questions.question: What does @Primary do?
options: Makes a bean load first at start-up
Marks the default bean when several beans of the same type exist
Hides all other beans of the type
questions.explanation: @Primary tells Spring which candidate to inject when no more specific instruction is given.

questions.question: Which one wins when a parameter has @Qualifier("smsSender") and another bean of the type is @Primary?
questions.explanation: The qualifier is the more specific instruction, so it overrides the default.

questions.question: EmailSender is @Primary, SmsSender and WhatsAppSender are plain beans, and List<NotificationSender> is injected into a runner. What does all.size() print?
questions.explanation: @Primary affects single injection only; a list still contains every bean of the type.

questions.question: Both EmailSender and SmsSender carry @Primary and AppointmentService asks for NotificationSender. What happens?
options: Spring uses the one declared first
Start-up fails because Spring cannot choose between two primary beans
The class with the shorter name wins
questions.explanation: Only one bean per type may be primary, so two primary beans still leave the choice ambiguous.

questions.question: A developer puts @Primary on the NotificationSender interface and expects EmailSender to become the default. Why does it not work?
options: Interfaces cannot have annotations at all
@Primary must go on the implementation class or the @Bean method
questions.explanation: The annotation marks a bean, so it belongs on the bean's class or the method that creates it.
